newsitem.title: ROMANIA: World Bank says release imminent for Romania loan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank says release imminent for Romania loan.

text.p: A World Bank credit tranche of $80 million to help Romania's new centrist government restructure industry should be released by the end of the week, the Bank's resident representative in Bucharest said on Friday.

Francois Ettori said the funds, part of a Financial and Enterprise Structural Adjustment Loan (FESAL), had been discussed by the Bank's board earlier this week when $550 million in other credits were approved.
Board members, he said, had until Friday to oppose resuming disbursement of the FESAL and objections were unlikely.

"Any objections would probably have been expressed at the long Board session and there was not a single hint of this," Ettori told Reuters. "Therefore it is most likely that by tomorrow if none are received it will be done."

About $100 million of the $280 million FESAL credit had been disbursed last year when the World Bank suspended credits to Romania, saying the leftist government of the time had failed to meet reform commitments.
Ettori said the final $100 million tranche of the credit was subject to the new administration meeting a series of targets, probably within the next 12 months.
These included the privatisation of 850 companies, 50 of them larger enterprises, plus two state banks.

Ettori praised the government's efforts to meet the demands of Western investors, including the long-awaited adoption on Wednesday of a law on portfolio investment and measures to restructure large state-run utilities.
"The targets for the $80 million have been largely met," he said. "If you like, the glass is more than half full. It's not 100 percent full, but more than half full."
The IMF approved fresh credits of $430 million earlier this year after endorsing the new government's reform programme.
